findings: src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:331: the change is one line. For any join whose build side is a LOGICAL_DELIM_GET, build_side_has_filter is now true. It used to be IsFiltering(children[0]), which tested the probe side. Nothing in the new condition refers to a particular query, table, literal or data distribution. It applies to every decorrelated correlated subquery whose inner join is built from the DELIM_GET.

Correctness: this flag only lets the existing Bloom filter mechanism be considered. A Bloom filter only drops probe rows that have no build match. The join-type gating earlier in GenerateJoinFilters (no MARK/ANTI/LEFT/OUTER/SINGLE) is unchanged, so no join type that needs unmatched probe rows can lose them. NULL and NOT DISTINCT FROM handling stays in the existing PushBloomFilter path. Nothing new can return wrong answers.

Cost: when the DELIM set covers the whole key domain, the filter is unselective. The existing CanUseBloomFilter checks (probe estimate larger than build count, COMPARE_EQUAL, not a perfect hash table) and the selectivity-based self-disable limit that cost. The change does not move work elsewhere or touch measurement code.
The change missed its stated target: q17 showed no gain. The measured gain is on q22, -19..-27%. This is still a legitimate general improvement.
